transcript.answer: No. Setting a fallback model (FALLBACK_MODEL_ID) and passing `resilience` to HAL Engine does not give you failover. HAL Engine fails over only through `fallbackProviders`. Its `resilience` setting is a retry policy and has no fallback field. Before the fix in issue #474 and PR #475, `buildEngine` in apps/api/src/server.ts passed `createHalEngine` a `provider` and no `fallbackProviders`. The fallback was checked against the allowlist and named in the `api.model` startup line, but it was never tried. The fix passes the resolved fallback as the only entry of `fallbackProviders`, or an empty list when FALLBACK_MODEL_ID is unset. Only the mock row can currently be a fallback, because a real fallback needs a chosen vendor (KU-07). The mock is also refused as a fallback when the primary model is real.

judgements.reason: The answer says resilience is only a retry policy, that failover happens only through fallbackProviders which buildEngine never passed, and that a mock fallback is refused behind a real primary; it omits only the echo rationale and contradicts nothing.
